geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Swing a compass arc to cut a ray in two places.

Goal: I can give a counterexample showing SSA is not a congruence test.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
SSA is not a congruence test. Take angle A = 30 degrees, AB = 10 and BC = 6. Draw the ray from A, then swing a compass arc of radius 6 from B. It crosses the ray at two points, C1 and C2. Triangles ABC1 and ABC2 both have the given side, side and angle, but they are not congruent.

When the given side opposite the angle is at least as long as the other given side, the arc crosses the ray only once on the correct side, and the triangle is fixed. That special case is behind HL in 5.12.

slides.title: Try it
slides.html:
Build SSA and see the two possible triangles.

Use the controls in the panel. Drag the hollow points on the board.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: With angle A = 30 degrees and AB = 10, what length of BC gives exactly one right triangle?
slides.reveal: BC = 5, the distance from B to the ray, since sin 30 degrees = 1/2. (The arc just touches the ray.)
